If any of these already-created custom animations fits better than a standard topic, use it instead by setting "libraryAnimation" to its exact name below (keep "topic" set too, so a sensible daily rhythm can still be estimated):
Ask me about anything – I\'ve grouped it by topic.
What happens when I tap the clock?

Then the app switches to a full-screen bedside display. Handy on a nightstand, but the screen stays on the whole time, which uses noticeably more battery. Tap anywhere to leave. What you see there depends on the mode: in Clock only the clock, in Routine I appear when a reminder is due, in Play I am there the whole time.
How is a reminder actually built?

Every reminder has four parts: what to do, a time window (like 8am–8pm), how often I nudge you inside that window, and – optionally – a daily goal. The nudges themselves don\'t count toward anything; only how many times you actually feed me inside your goal does.
What\'s the difference between the interval and the daily goal?

The interval is just how often I tap you on the shoulder – it can be as tight as every minute. The daily goal is what actually counts: set it to 4 and 4 of 4 is done, no matter how many extra nudges I gave you in between.
What does the time window do?
I only nudge you inside that window, e.g. 9am–5pm. Outside it, that reminder stays completely quiet, even once its interval would technically be due again.
Why are my \"open duration\" choices limited?
They only go up to the reminder\'s own interval – one that nudges you every minute can only stay open up to a minute. That way it can never still be sitting there once its own next nudge is due.
What happens when two reminders are due at the same moment?

I show them one after another instead of merging them or moving either one to a different time – whichever has the shorter interval goes first. You\'ll see them appear back-to-back rather than exactly on their own schedule.
What happens if I don\'t feed a reminder right away?

It stays open for as long as its \"open duration\" says – never longer than its own interval. While it\'s open and unfed, though, I don\'t check on any OTHER reminders at all, so it can still hold up whatever else is due until you respond or it times out.
Can a reminder just… not show up?

Yes, on purpose. If I was busy with another open reminder and your reminder\'s moment slipped more than about 90 seconds into the past by the time I got back to it, I won\'t show it late – I quietly line it up for its next slot instead. Showing something noticeably late felt worse than skipping it once. A reminder with a long interval and a long open duration is the most likely one to cause this for a more frequent reminder waiting behind it.
Can the same reminder nudge me twice in a row?
No – I never show the same reminder again before its own interval has fully passed, even if something tries to trigger it early.
Why didn\'t I get a nudge even though nothing seemed to be blocking it?
I only nudge you while your screen is on. If it\'s off right when one\'s due, I skip that occurrence instead of saving it for later – same reasoning as above: better honest than stale.
How long does an animation actually play?
Exactly as long as its open duration says – a quick 8-second flash by default, or longer if you\'ve set that. Feeding me always ends it early, whatever the setting.
Can I use my own animation instead of the built-in ones?
Yes – pick one from the animation library when creating or editing a reminder. A library animation is shown instead of the topic\'s default one.
I have a star left over – how do I spend it in the skill tree?

Every level-up earns one star. Open the skill tree (the button under your companion) and tap any highlighted node marked \"next up\" – that works the same for a whole group and for a single animation. Tapping spends the star and unlocks it; tap the same spot again afterward to open it and see what\'s now reachable underneath.
How do I actually respond to a reminder?
Drag the clock onto me, or use the feed gesture – that\'s how you tell me you did the thing.
Does every reminder affect your mood?

Only if you\'ve turned that on – it\'s off by default (Settings → Mood affects behaviour), so trying the app out never feels like managing anyone\'s feelings. Switched on, only reminders with an actual daily goal count; leave one at \"No goal\" and it stays a pure nudge either way.
What happens to my reminders if I switch avatar?
Each avatar keeps its own set of reminders. Switching avatar switches which set is active – the others are still there, just paused, waiting for you to switch back.

What are Clock, Routine and Play?

Three ways to run me, chosen top left. Clock: just the clock, nothing else. Routine: your own reminders – I show up when one is due. Play: I live in my own little world and go about my day. Each step to the right adds something.

The dock shows the clock and nothing else – no me, no rooms. Reminders rest while it is on, and nothing is recorded either: without me there would be no way to answer them, so they would only pile up as things you supposedly skipped. Switch back to Routine and they carry on exactly where they were.
Your own reminders run. When one is due I turn up next to the clock – drag the clock onto me to say you have done it. That is the mode this app was built around.

I am there the whole time and live through a day of my own: I sleep, go to work, do the shopping, take a walk. Your own reminders keep running as always – on top of them one is drawn at random, and feeding that earns experience, coins and meals. Tap me and I will tell you how things stand.
Do my habits change what you do in Play mode?

Yes, and that is the point of it. Whatever you have set yourself and not yet done today pulls me towards it – I reach for that more often on my own. Tap me and I will tell you what I am watching out for.
Turn it on in Settings, then two buttons appear at the top right of Play mode: a circle for a film, a viewfinder for a single picture. Films run up to 90 seconds and you decide when to stop.
Where do the recordings end up?

In the collection under Settings, films and pictures together, newest first. From there you can share them or put them in your phone gallery – that step is deliberate, so nothing lands in your gallery unasked.
On purpose. Social apps replace the sound anyway, and music would raise licensing questions that a small app should not have.
What can you actually tell me?

What is really there: what you have looked after today, how the week has gone, what you set yourself, and what is still open. I make nothing up – everything I say comes from your own data, and nothing leaves the phone for it.

Right now you are in Play mode: I am there the whole time and live a day of my own. Your own reminders keep running as always – on top of them I turn up by myself now and then, and feeding that earns experience, coins and meals.

I live here: I sleep, go to work, do the shopping, take a walk. Feed me and it earns experience, coins and a meal in the larder. Whatever you have set yourself and not yet done today pulls me towards it.

A short motif when you answer a reminder, on a level-up and when someone visits. Every creature sounds different. Silent at night, and never over music that is playing.

I am Puffling. I deliver parcels – and I keep taking detours, because there is always something new lying about.
My bed stands against the wall with the picture. I did not choose it, it was already hanging there. I like it anyway.
At my workbench I build things out of what is left over. Little of it ever gets finished. That is fine.
I have known Gloop the longest. He is slower than me – and when I am with him, so am I.
My park is mown and has a bench. Nothing special. But I know where everything is there.

Sometimes I set off and halfway there I forget where to. Then I sit on the bench until it comes back to me. Starlet found me there once. She did not ask why, she just sat down until it came back to me.
The forest starts behind the street. I rarely go in – not out of fear. It is so quiet that you can hear yourself.
The other day I waited outside a stranger\'s door for a while, just because there was a pile of chestnuts I wanted to count. In the end there were twenty-one. The delivery still arrived on time.
I am Starlet. I raise plants. Some do not make it, and that is part of it.
I sleep in a hammock. When I turn over, half the room sways along.
Most of all I like sitting in my swing and watching nothing happen outside.
Hootlet and I hardly ever talk. Sometimes we just sit next to each other, and that is enough for both of us.
I mow nothing on my meadow. Everything may grow as it likes – including what nobody planted.
I often forget what I was looking for. Instead I find other things on the way.
On some nights the moon hangs low over the meadow. Then I stay outside longer than I meant to.
Yesterday I watched a snail cross the flower bed for a while. It did not get far, but it was not in a hurry either.
I am Wyrmling. In the gym I show people the first step. The second one they think of themselves.
I sleep in a nest of twigs. Next to it lies what I have collected. You may touch all of it.
At the forge I hammer glowing iron. Not always does something come of it. The noise helps regardless.
Fennec looks after everyone. I keep telling him to look after himself too. He does not listen.
Outside my place it only goes up. From up there everything looks doable – that is why I climb.
I talk loudly. Partly so nobody notices when I am unsure.
In the evening the lights come on in the houses along the street. I do not know who lives there. I like it anyway. One light further up is not a house though – that is Hootlet, at the observatory.
This morning I restacked the mats in the gym, just because the old stack was leaning. Nobody asked for it. It looked better right away.
I am Fennec. I keep the beacon burning. Nobody notices when it works – that is the whole point.
I sleep in a den. Narrow, dark, warm. From inside you hear everything that passes outside.
I dig. Not to find something – I put things in places I will remember later.
Wyrmling is loud and means well. After he has been here, the room is emptier.
There is an acacia out in the savannah. You see it before you see the sand. I take my bearings from it.
I sleep badly when I do not know whether you are all right. That is why I ask.
The shop is closed at night. The lantern in front of it stays lit though. Somebody must have switched it on.

At the beacon I replaced the wick today, even though the old one would have lasted a while longer. Better before than in the middle of it. Gloop would probably have let the old one burn until it went out on its own.
I am Gloop. In the bakery I wait until the dough is ready. There is no hurrying it.
I sleep in a hollow on the floor. I cannot get up high, and I do not miss anything.
I turn clay. I have no fixed shape myself – perhaps that is why I like giving one to something else.
Puffling comes by often and talks fast. I understand half of it. It is the good half.
Outside my place everything is soft. You sink in a little. You also come back out.
I do not tidy up. The bowls stay where I put them down. They are in nobody’s way.
When it rains you can hear it inside at the window. That is my favourite weather.
A lump of clay flew off my wheel today and stuck to the ceiling. I am leaving it up there for now. Maybe it will come down on its own.
I am Hootlet. At the observatory I note down what changes in the sky. Mostly nothing changes.
I sleep in a hollow trunk. From there I can see the door without anybody seeing me.
I play the wind harp. Talking is not my strength. This works better.
Starlet sits down beside me sometimes. She asks nothing, and I have to explain nothing.
My forest is not dark at night. You only have to keep still long enough for your eyes to notice.
I know a lot and say little. Both come easily to me. One may be the reason for the other.
There is a shooting star that comes rarely. I do not wait for it. I am simply always there when it comes.
The sky was overcast today. Nothing to note down. I stayed anyway.
That is all I know about myself right now. Ask me again later.
That is all that comes to me today. Ask me again tomorrow.
You keep me moving. I am outside more than in.
Since you send me off, I know the way to the street in the dark.
I notice where I have already been. The forest behind the street is no longer strange.
I no longer set off because you say so. I set off because it is time.
With you it is about looking after things. I watch out – for me and for you.
By now I put something out for myself before I need it.
When I do not hear from you for a while, I go to the kitchen anyway. For later.
By now I can tell when a day was hard on you. Do not ask me how.
With you things go quiet. I sit more than I walk.
I stay seated longer than I meant to. That is new.
By now I hear the rain before I see it.
I no longer need anything in order to be somewhere. I am simply there.
With you things get finished. I always have something on the go.
There is always something half-started in my corner now.
I tidy the workbench in the evening. So it can go on tomorrow.
The first piece I ever finished stands in my room. Do not ask what it is.
I cannot say yet. I do not know you well enough.
You do a bit of everything. So do I – I am not settling on one thing.
